sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r8/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 35 (#34) and Internal Quality Checks row 35 (#34), no cell comments
evidence: Every interactive, time-varying or viewport promise in the public notes has a criterion telling the judge to perform the action or wait rather than score first paint. Keyboard: polish enter_sends (Shift+Enter then Enter) and escape_closes (press Escape, then reload). Confirm: delete_confirm (decline, reload, then confirm). Time waits: link_highlight ('still highlighted about ten seconds later'), refusal_in_place ('wait about ten seconds without touching anything'), and functional wall_added_live / unread_and_new_messages_line / live_updates_keep_my_work ('without reloading, within about ten seconds', using two browser contexts, with the draft, open reply box and scroll position checked after the remote changes). Typing '@' to get suggestions and picking one is in wall_mentions_and_links Part B. The stale edit across two contexts is in edits_and_stale_edit. Timer and hold changes are driven through controls with the fixed clock (timer_changes, hold_scope_and_release, deleted_and_expired_messages Part B), so no real-time expiry wait is needed. Viewport: the visual prompt says 'resize to 1440 by 900 first, and to 390 by 844 for the phone criterion' (visual/prompt.md Task state). matter_sidebar is at desktop width, phone_chambers at 390x844, and polish transcript_print is 'At 390 by 844' with an explicit documentElement.scrollWidth check. The brief has no theming or animation requirement, so no toggle is needed. A sample weak app that ignores the timing (a toast-only refusal, a highlight that fades after a few seconds, live updates only on reload, an M-12 list that stays after a live wall) fails a named step. I found no conforming alternative that the instructed actions would wrongly fail. The '~10 s' waits match the brief's 'within about ten seconds'. Residual notes, not defects for this row: (a) link_highlight samples at ~10 s, so a highlight that fades after, say, 30 s would pass even though the brief says it 'stays until you open something else'; (b) the 390 px no-sideways-scroll rule for the main thread page is only judged through the likert visual phone_chambers anchors ('fit the width'), with no binary scrollWidth check like the one transcript_print has. Risk is true because raw-evidence-index.json says that no full configured judge run exists on these bytes. The only runtime evidence is the scripted golden functional.cjs, which does wait 10 s (lines 697, 720), set a 390x844 viewport (line 709) and press keys (660-663). That shows the steps can be done, not that the claude-code/GLM judge actually performs them. The visual dimension is not covered by any run.
